title: fix(objectql)!: a multi-valued reference element is held to the single value's stored form (#22908)
body:
Fixes #22908
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

Two queue builds of this PR went red on the suite-duration ceiling gate (#22949), over packages this diff does not touch. The queue kept the entry, and a third build landed it. A park line written here in error is withdrawn.

## What changed

`packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts`, the multi-value branch of `validateOne`. It returned `null` early for `lookup` / `user` / `file` / `image` ("reference integrity is handled elsewhere"), so an element of a `multiple: true` field was never parsed against its stored form. Those types now fall through to the ADR-0104 value-shape arm that a single value goes through. That arm parses the whole array with `valueSchemaFor(def, 'stored')`, which is already `z.array(element)` for a multi-valued field (`ReferenceIdValueSchema` for `lookup` / `user`, `FileReferenceIdValueSchema` for `file` / `image`). The result is the same refusal (`invalid_type`, message key `invalid_value_shape`), under the same posture, with the same warn-first sink. No second shape rule was added, as triage 6115825886 binds.

- One predicate, `isValueShapeJudgedType`, now answers "does the ADR-0104 arm judge this type" in all three places that ask it: the arm, the multi-value branch that hands an element to it, and `valueShapeViolation` (the scan's predicate). Before this, the scan and the branch could disagree about which types those are.
- `valueShapeDetail` names the index of the wrong element on a multi-valued field (`at index 1: ...`), so a refusal names the field and the index. The write path and `os migrate value-shapes` share this one reading. `repeater` / `vector` details are unchanged.
- System principal: the shape check is the validator's, which already runs for an `isSystem` write, so the system door now refuses too. `assertReferencesResolve` is untouched (read-only): its `isSystem` latitude on whether an id EXISTS stays as #4551 left it, and a test pins that.
- `file` / `image` with `multiple: true`: measured and given their own stored form, the opaque `sys_file` id, under the media posture (`mediaValueShapeStrict` / the file-references flag). A verified media flag does not open reference elements, and the value-shapes flag does not open media elements (pinned).

One changeset, `.changeset/22908-multi-reference-element-shape.md`: `@objectstack/objectql` `minor`, BREAKING (accept-set narrowing), ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, FROM / TO stated.

## Premise, checked on `origin/main` `018b077fbf` before any edit

- At the validator: with `valueShapeStrict: true`, `{ team: [{ id: 'x' }], watchers: [false] }` on a multi-valued `lookup` / `user` was ADMITTED, while the single-valued control `{ owner: { id: 'x' } }` was refused `invalid_type`.
- At claim, read-only (triage's item). Does ADR-0104's value-shapes scan report a stored multi-valued element of the wrong shape? Yes. `scanValueShapes` over rows `team: [{ id }]`, `team: [false]`, `watchers: [42]` reported `team` count 2 and `watchers` count 1, plus a single-valued control row, with `blocking` 4. So no gap card is owed. But at BASE the scan counted values the strict write path admitted, which contradicts the scan's own header ("count exactly what strict mode would reject"). This change closes that disagreement, and a test pins the two in agreement. The media half has its own evidence: `backfill-file-references.ts` converts arrays element by element.

## Pins (tests beside the code)

- `packages/objectql/src/validation/multi-reference-element-shape.test.ts` (validator level): for `lookup` / `user` with `multiple: true`, the three bad elements (boolean, number, embedded record) are refused on insert and update, naming the field and index 0. The wrong element at index 2 is named as index 2. CONTROLS: the single-valued rows refuse the same three with no index; a well-formed id array and `[]` are accepted; a non-array is still the array refusal. A readonly multi-valued reference is judged by its shape, as a readonly single value is. Warn-first admits the element and reports it to the sink (`value-shape` gate for references, `media` for files). The gate split holds, and the `OS_ALLOW_LAX_VALUE_SHAPES` hatch still works. `file` / `image` elements are held to the `sys_file` id form. The scan predicate and the strict write path agree on every probe.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-multi-reference-element-shape.test.ts` (engine write path, strict posture): the three bad elements on `lookup` and `user` with `multiple: true`, through a caller's context (the engine call the REST data routes make) and the system principal, on insert and update. Each is refused as a `ValidationError` with `code` `VALIDATION_FAILED` and `fields[0]` `{ field, code: 'invalid_type' }`, and nothing is stored or changed. CONTROLS: the single-valued rows are unchanged on both doors; well-formed id arrays are accepted on both doors; and a well-formed id that names no row is `reference_not_found` for the caller but still written by the system principal (the `isSystem` existence latitude is kept).

## The real door: PR #22907's reference-shape family (one-off, not committed)

`runReferenceShapeProofs` from `@objectstack/verify` (a real `bootStack`, the REST data routes as the signed-in caller, and `hooks.run` with `{ system: true }`) over a fixture with `accounts` (lookup, multiple), `watchers` (user, multiple), and single-valued `account` / `assignee` controls. It ran as a scratch test file that was deleted afterwards. It resolves `@objectstack/objectql` through its `exports`, so through the built `dist/`.

- Fixed build: 4 fields, 4 proven, 0 holes; 48 probes, 48 refused `invalid_type` (REST answers `400`), 0 admitted, 0 unattributed.
- Ablated build (below): the two multi-valued fields read `holes`, 8 of 12 admitted each. That reproduces the card's measurement: REST embedded record admitted `201` / `200`; REST boolean / number refused only as `reference_not_found` `400`; system door all admitted. The single-valued controls stay proven. Summary: 2 proven, 2 holes, 32 refused, 16 admitted.

## Ablation (one-off; `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, plus an EXIT/INT/TERM trap)

- Mutation: the early return restored as `if (isValueShapeJudgedType(t) && String('ABLATION-22908-MARKER')) return null;` ahead of the option arm. Anchor 1 to 0, blob `671387d31cbd` to `7cc631fd7095`. On disk: marker 1, the early-return line 1.
- objectql pins (src-resolved): 43 failed, 10 passed (53). The 10 that pass are the controls.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql build`, then `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs`: the marker is present in 4 dist files. The real-door reading is above.
- Restore: `git checkout HEAD -- ABS_PATH` by the tool. Blob after restore equals HEAD (`671387d31cbd`), `git diff HEAD` is empty, `git status` is clean. Rebuilt; `--absent` preflight: the marker is absent from all 14 dist files. objectql pins 53/53 pass; the real-door reading is 48/48 refused.
- First attempt was a no-op: the tool refused before the child ran, because my replacement still contained the anchor (count 1 to 1). It restored to the HEAD blob and took no reading. The second attempt is the one reported.

## Local verification

All read at the final head, `55cf89916e`, after the last commit.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 405 files passed, 7911 tests passed (through `os-verify-lock`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` and `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0, test layer held at 40 files / 234 errors / 65 pinned signatures, with no new signature. Both new test files are in the `tsconfig.test.json` program (`--listFiles`); `tsconfig.json` excludes tests.
- Gates: the 69 commands derived at dispatch for the declared surface all exit 0. Re-derived on the real diff (`dispatch-gates --commands`, change set from the merge base): 66 families, all inside the 69. `dispatch-gates --ran` with recorded exit codes: 66 derived, 66 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN (a derived zero). The 3 extra are engine-surface families: `check:error-status-conformance`, `check:stack-collection-maps`, `check:swallow-census-controls`. One gate went red during development, `check:objectql-double-limit`, which was right: the new engine test's stub `find` ignored the caller's `limit`. It now applies the bound after the filter.
- The dist-reading gates (`check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:published-files`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`, `check-dts-emitted --self-test`) ran after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql build`.
- Lint, narrowed and proven: eslint's own config (`calculateConfigForFile`) applies to all 3 changed `.ts` files, and none is ignored. `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over them gave 3 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed rules), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- Consumers: no export, spec key or response shape changes, so no import-side suites were run. A grep of downstream writers of multi-valued arrays (`plugin-approvals` attachments, `service-storage` gallery, `rest` and `runtime` fixtures, the showcase seed) found id elements only. CI runs the full set.

## Acceptance notes (observations; not filed)

- The spec's authoring-time default-value gate (`actionableValueIssueMessage`, `packages/spec/src/data/default-value-shape.ts`) is a deliberately separate reading. It does not name the index for a multi-valued literal default. That is polish, not a defect class; carrier: none.
- `assertReferencesResolve`'s note "already-expanded objects are skipped" now describes a path reachable only under warn-first. On a strict deployment the validator refuses an expanded element first, for both cardinalities, as it already did for a single value.
- Not measured: what the console (`objectui`) writes into a multi-valued lookup / user / file / image on save. No `objectui` checkout was available here. If a console editor wrote expanded records back as elements, a strict deployment would now refuse that save. The single-valued field has refused that shape under the same posture all along.
- ⛔ Not folded here, per triage: making `os verify --reference-shapes` the default. The one-off reading above is the input for that separate call. `examples/app-showcase` itself was not run through the CLI.
